motivation: Release-only relief A primarily reduced table support while welded, barely changing the free-box release state: in two known overruns +0.006–0.016mm mean face position, +0.19–0.41mm/s speed. In clone checks the first force was more sensitive to actual release velocity than this actuator provided. Both excessive peaks remained on detachment, whereas the two A failure cases first touched 3.852/3.855s versus 3.847–3.848 for exposed passing sh3/sh5. Instead prepare the approach/settling transient with more time *under the still-closed weld*. Do not advance actual release.
mechanism: From the original terminal descent, take only the world-z progression of the TCP a fraction of a support blend ahead; keep original x/y/orientation. Lead is half of the frozen hybrid 20ms transition, raised C2 over the first half of the 300ms descent, kept to 50ms before release, then tapered back to zero by scheduled release. Cap the normal displacement smoothly at one quarter of the existing 8mm pose-correction bound. The displacement is applied via full pose IK calibrated once per reset and stored as neutral additive joint deltas. No new postrelease action, case-specific switch or plant labels, no update for zero payload. Refined height registration and early horizontal inertia are unchanged. This differs from a whole-arm fast/hold or a changed release clock.
qualification: No slope/threshold/amplitude selection on qualified outcomes; stage-matched protected costs (<=1.05 versus both R10 and incumbent R15), FA (20ms one-to-one), original G4, tool/saturation preserved. 22 exposed cases, disjoint normal+unloaded, then fresh paired forced/no-force+known sentinel only if both previous stages qualify. Time reported separately. No retuning on fresh or impacts.
